input.title: The Adyghe School in Syria
input.notes: The Adyghe Private School was established in Qunaitra, Syria, in 1932 and continued operating until 1942. It was the first Circassian elementary school in the diaspora where the entire curriculum was taught in the Circassian language, except for Arabic language classes.

examples.description: A 20th-century photograph from Qunaitra, Syria showing the Adyghe School. The school was established in 1932 and continued operating until 1942. It was the first Circassian elementary school in the diaspora where the entire curriculum was taught in the Circassian language except for Arabic language classes.

input.title: Cherkes Ethem
input.notes: Cherkes Ethem (1886–1948) was a prominent Circassian guerrilla leader who became a vital militia commander in the early stages of the Turkish War of Independence. Leading the irregular Kuvâ-yi Seyyâre (Mobile Forces), he initially earned national acclaim for stalling the Greek military advance and suppressing internal anti-revolutionary rebellions. However, his independent stance and refusal to merge his forces into the newly established regular Turkish army led to a bitter conflict with the central Ankara government. Declared a traitor and rebel in late 1920, he was defeated and spent the remainder of his life in exile.

examples.description: A photograph from around 1920, from Türkiye, in the Circassian diaspora, featuring Cherkes Ethem (1886–1948), a Circassian guerrilla leader who commanded the irregular Kuvâ-yi Seyyâre (Mobile Forces) in the early stages of the Turkish War of Independence. Declared a traitor and rebel in late 1920, he was defeated and spent the remainder of his life in exile.
